Works when the masthead is visible and when it auto-hides on scroll down (F023): the button sits directly under the masthead when shown and moves up to the viewport top (small gap) when hidden, with no overlap and no large empty gap. Light and dark; 375/768/1280/1900 widths. Author sidebar untouched.
steps: Cause: _post-ux.scss ~line 138 forces `.page__content > .sidebar__right.sticky` to position: static (F059). Change it to position: sticky; top: <masthead offset>; z-index above content, keeping width auto, transparent, no border/shadow, margin as now. Sticky only works if no ancestor between it and the scroll root has overflow hidden/auto; check .page__content/.page and fix (overflow: visible) if needed.

Offset: masthead is `html.masthead-autohide .masthead {position: sticky; top:0}` and toggles `.is-hidden` (translateY(-100%)) in assets/js/post-ux.js (~line 293). Expose masthead height as a CSS variable (e.g. --pux-mast-h set from mast.offsetHeight on load/resize) and a state hook (e.g. html class `masthead-hidden` toggled alongside .is-hidden in the same update function). CSS: top: calc(var(--pux-mast-h) + 8px) normally, top: 8px when masthead hidden, with a transition matching the masthead (0.25s, none under prefers-reduced-motion). If JS/autohide is absent, fall back to top: 8px offset below a static masthead (sticky stays within viewport).

Verify in browser: open /blog/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection-wrap-up/ at 1280, scroll 1500px down then up: button stays visible and left-aligned with its original x (same as before scrolling, compare getBoundingClientRect().left); when masthead is hidden button top <= 16px; when masthead shown button top >= masthead bottom and does not overlap it. Repeat at 375 and 768 and in dark (data-theme=dark). Scroll back to top: button returns to its normal place above the first paragraph. Page scrollWidth == viewport. Button must not stay sticky past the end of the post content (no overlap with footer/prev-next).
